card: This PR refactors block and undo file flushing in BlockManager to encapsulate file-level flushing and error notification into a single FlushFile helper, ensuring any flush failure invariably triggers the flush-error notification. It solves the risk of future code paths reporting a flush failure to FlushStateToDisk without properly initiating node shutdown via AbortNode. Unit tests are added to verify that both block and undo flush failures trigger notifications. It is a defensive internal refactor that builds on top of PR 35714.
evidence: PR description: 'A future flush source (a new file type, a new error branch) that sets success = false without notifying would make FlushStateToDisk() return an error without AbortNode().'
problem: When `FlushChainstateBlockFile()` fails, callers such as `FlushStateToDisk()` rely on the invariant that a fatal flush-error notification (which initiates node shutdown) has already been fired. Today, this invariant depends on each individual branch in `FlushBlockFile` and `FlushUndoFile` remembering to invoke the notification before returning failure, creating a risk that future flush code paths return an error without triggering node shutdown.
scope_notes: Includes commits from PR #35714 in its branch history.
summary: Couples disk flush operations with flush-error notification handling by introducing a private `BlockManager::FlushFile()` helper in `blockstorage.cpp`. Replaces individual flush and notification calls across block and undo file flushes with this helper to guarantee that any failed file flush emits a notification. Adds unit tests exercising separate block and undo file flush failures to verify notification behavior.
